newsitem.title: USA: U.S. weekly cash lumber review - Feb 28.
newsitem.headline: U.S. weekly cash lumber review - Feb 28.

text.p: Random Lengths Gross List Cash Lumber Prices Quotes:
(2x4 Std&Btr) WEEKLY MIDWEEK PREV WK YR AGO

COMMENT - Conflicting opinions about the course of trading abounded this week, leaving the market floundering for direction, Random Lengths said in its end-week review. Retailers and secondaries replenished cautiously through Thursday, convinced that a hand to mouth strategy remained best for now.

Producers gave ground on prices when they had to but clung to the opinion that there was nothing wrong with the market that a dose of good spring weather wouldn't cure. Wholesalers pushed to pare offering lists in the waning days of the month, often undercutting mill quotes, the lumber reporting agency said.
Confusion surrounding the final weeks of the first year of the U.S.-Canada lumber agreement weighed heavily on the market.

Concern that Canadian shipments to the U.S. would rise sharply when the quota year ends on March 31 was widespread on the buying side. But producers reminded traders that the feared "wall of wood" failed to materialize last year, it said.

Rain across the South bottled up wood in treaters' and dealers' yards, contributing to the market's slowness. But the wet weather also slowed logging and more southern mills announced log-related cutbacks or temporary closures.
A sag in lumber futures that contributed to a drop in Western S-P-F 2x4 kept buyers on edge, Random Lengths said.

Others cited Fed chairman Greeespan's warning that interest rates might have to rise to keep a lid on the economy. But most retailers acknowledged that there was a solid volume of business in the pipeline waiting to start when weather permits. Only a few end-of-month bargains surfaced at mills, it said.
Trading in boards was less intense but many 12-inch items continued their ascent, Random Lengths said.
Canadian exports as of February 20 were at 60.8 percent of Jan-March fee-free quota and 92.5 pct of annual quota, it said.
